notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.
Added a dedicated media_wall cluster because the brief explicitly requests a TV facing the bed and names media wall as the likely primary focus.
Kept the object program minimal while preserving bedroom essentials and circulation.
Nightstands remain optional with a max of 2; work/lounge/utility remain conditional.
Bedroom is 18.21 m2 with clear wall anchors and a strong media-wall brief, so bed, wardrobe, and tv console should survive longer than optional support clusters.
Nightstands are desirable but should remain flexible: keep up to two only when circulation around the bed stays comfortable.
Work-study, lounge-reading, and utility items are low priority for this room and should drop early unless surplus is unusually high.
Media wall is useful here because the brief explicitly requests a tv facing the bed; prefer a compact tv console to preserve openness.
Preserved bed-to-TV facing intent and kept entry clearance off the bed zone.
Prioritized privacy back zone for sleep and solid-wall anchors for storage/media.
Kept center openness and circulation clear as a shared constraint.
Request contract LLM mode enabled via TKNT_REQUEST_CONTRACT_LLM; deterministic validation remains active.
SemanticLayoutPlanner used the room profile registry as the canonical rule source.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Bedroom correction raised restfulness and clutter control.
